name: Blackberry & black raspberry
scientific: Rubus allegheniensis, R. occidentalis, R. armeniacus and other Rubus spp.
habitat: Thorny arching canes in old fields, forest edges, powerline cuts, fencerows and clearcuts; the invasive Himalayan blackberry forms enormous thickets across the Northwest and California.
parts: Ripe fruit eaten raw or cooked. Black raspberries ripen first (late June-July) and go dull black; blackberries follow (July into September) and are only sweet once they turn from shiny to dull matte black and detach with no pull. Red-stage fruit is just sour, not poisonous.
harvest: There are no toxic aggregate-drupelet fruits in North America — every Rubus produces edible fruit — which makes this the safest entry on the list. The practical rule is to watch what else is growing through the thicket (poison ivy, and Virginia creeper's blue-black berries on coral-red stalks, which NC State rates high-severity) so nothing else ends up in the bucket. Canes are biennial: pick the fruit, don't trample or cut this year's green primocanes or you lose next year's crop. Leave the lower and interior fruit for birds and bears.
